author: Boeckers, Anja; Brinkmann, Anke; Jerg-Bretzke, Lucia; Lamp, Christoph; Traue, Harald C.; Boeckers, Tobias M.

title: Rapid communication: Sex differences in artificial grammar learning: Evidence for different strategies in men and women
abstract: Investigated differences in classification performance of women and men during artificial-grammar learning (AGL). Participants were 65 college students (mean age 22 years): 34 women and 31 men. Results show that women's and men's responses correspond to a large extent. Consistent differences, however, were found in a variable that codes overlaps between training and test items in terms of string fragments: chunk strength. It is concluded that these findings are best explained by the assumption that women and men apply different cognitive strategies at test.
author: Lotz, Anja; Kinder, Annette

title: Tacit guidance for collaborative multimedia learning
abstract: Investigated whether a computer generated collaboration integration tool benefits individual and collaborative learning efforts during dyadic collaborative multimedia learning. Participants (40 college students mean age 22 years) were assigned to 2 experimental groups: the individual support only group and the individual and collaborative support group. The study consisted of 5 phases including training phase, individual learning phase, test phase 1, collaborative learning phase, and test phase 2. The tool was compared experimentally with an integration task that has already been shown to foster meaningful individual learning processes. Findings reveal that providing group awareness can lead to better individual learning gains by reducing demanding processes and by tacitly guiding learner interactions, thereby saving cognitive capacities for meaningful individual and collaborative processes.
author: Bodemer, Daniel

title: Trainings in Mensch-Maschine-Systemen : Strategien zur Unterstützung des Erwerbs mentaler Kausalmodelle
abstract: Based on theories of causal knowledge acquisition, a framework for mental causal model acquisition of complex technical systems was developed. This framework forms the basis for the examination of relevant multimedia design principles. In close dependence on the framework, didactic strategies for computer-based knowledge transfer and multimedia psychology principles are presented and discussed. These strategies and the framework provide the basis for the deduction of a training concept for the enhancement of causal mental model acquisition. In three empirical studies different training strategies have been developed and tested. The focus was on the effects of the training strategies on the performance in system interaction and in knowledge tests, both forming indicators for the quality of the mental causal model. The simulation of a technical system served as experimental platform. Study 1 investigated holistic, gradual, and text-based training strategies, combined with a varying degree of learner participation. The results concerning system knowledge show a slight advantage of the holistic and gradual trainings over the text-based training, although there could be shown no differences concerning the cause-and-effect knowledge and the system performance. In Study 2, the presentation of the gradual training strategy was optimized and compared to a text-based training. As a second factor, the system interaction was varied. Results show that a combination of gradual visualization and system interaction has a positive influence on both knowledge acquisition and performance in system interaction. Study 3 investigated the influence of guided mental simulation (envisioning) compared to unguided system interaction. Results show that guided mental simulation is beneficial for the causal knowledge acquisition, yet there is no provided evidence for advantages for the performance in system interaction. of the training concept thus seems very promising. Möglichkeiten zur Gestaltung von computerbasierten Trainingsstrategien für Aufgaben in komplexen Mensch-Maschine-Systemen werden entwickelt und überprüft. Auf der Grundlage von Theorien zum kausalen Wissenserwerb wird zunächst ein Rahmenmodell zur Beschreibung des Erwerbs mentaler Kausalmodelle über komplexe technische Systeme entwickelt. Dieses Rahmenmodell dient als Grundlage für die Auseinandersetzung mit relevanten Multimedia-Prinzipien zur Gestaltung computerbasierter Trainingssysteme. In enger Anlehnung an die im Rahmenmodell beschriebenen Aspekte des Wissenserwerbs werden didaktische Strategien zur computerbasierten Wissensvermittlung sowie Prinzipien der Multimediapsychologie vorgestellt und diskutiert. Diese Strategien bilden, gemeinsam mit dem Rahmenmodell, die Grundlage für die Ableitung eines Trainingskonzepts zur Förderung des Erwerbs mentaler Kausalmodelle über komplexe technische Systeme. In drei empirischen Studien wurden, ausgehend von diesem Trainingskonzept, verschiedene Trainingsstrategien entwickelt und untersucht. Der Fokus lag auf den Auswirkungen der Trainingsstrategien auf die Leistungen bei der Systeminteraktion und bei der Wissensdiagnose. Als Versuchsumgebung diente die Simulation eines technischen Systems. In Studie 1 (79 Studierende im Alter von 19 bis 35 Jahren) wurden holistische und sukzessive Visualisierungsvarianten einem textbasierten Training gegenübergestellt. Zusätzlich wurde das Ausmaß an Lernerbeteiligung variiert. Die Ergebnisse zeigten einen leichten Vorteil der beiden Visualisierungsvarianten für die Unterstützung des Erwerbs von Systemwissen, jedoch keine Unterschiede im Erwerb von Ursache-Wirkungswissen und bei der Leistung in der Systeminteraktion. In Studie 2 (48 Studierende im Alter von 20 bis 40 Jahren) wurde die Darstellung der sukzessiven Visualisierungsvariante optimiert und einem textbasierten Training gegenübergestellt. Als ein weiterer Faktor wurde die Interaktion mit dem zu bedienenden System als Bestandteil des Trainings variiert. Es zeigte sich, dass eine Kombination aus Visualisierung und Systeminteraktion sowohl für den Wissenserwerb als auch für die Fähigkeit, ein technisches System zu bedienen, förderlich ist. In Studie 3 (34 Studierende im Alter von 19 bis 34 Jahren) wurde der Einfluss von mentaler Simulation (Envisioning) als Trainingsstrategie untersucht und einer Kontrollbedingung gegenübergestellt, in der die Probanden ohne mentale Simulation trainiert wurden. Es zeigte sich, dass die Anleitung von Envisioning-Prozessen Vorteile für den Erwerb von kausalen Wissensstrukturen gegenüber dem alleinigen Experimentieren bietet. Für die Leistung bei der Systeminteraktion hingegen konnten keine Vorteile der strukturierten Anleitung von Envisioning-Prozessen gegenüber der Kontrollbedingung gezeigt werden.
author: Klostermann, Anne

title: Rekodieren im Deutschen und Englischen: Wie rekodieren Englischlerner/-innen mit deutscher Muttersprache englische Wörter?
abstract: Conventional reading models, such as the dual-route-model or the connectionist model assume that recoding is the same in all orthographies. Empirical results, however, show that recoding is influenced by characteristics of orthography. In particular, the consistency of an orthography seems to play a central role in recoding. There are only few theories or models that take these results into account: the orthographic-depth-hypothesis (Katz & Frost, 1992), the psycholinguistic grain-size-theory (Ziegler & Goswami, 2005) and the two-cycles-model (Berent & Perfetti, 1995) which takes into account the inconsistency of English orthography. The empirical evidence behind these theories and models is different, but the results suggest unanimously that native English speakers use different (additional) recoding strategies to German native speakers. According to the grain-size-theory (Ziegler & Goswami, 2005) German readers recode new words using a grapheme-phoneme-mapping, whereas English readers also have to take into account larger units, such as onset and rime. Using onsets and rimes, they can form analogies to new words. The two-cycles-model (Berent & Perfetti, 1995) assumes that English natives initially only process the consonants of a word and integrate the vowels only in a second cycle that is slower and more controlled than the first. Such results are not taken into consideration in didactics of English as a second language very often. In general, prior knowledge based on German learners' experience of learning their own language is excluded from the English language instruction. Moreover, relevant recoding strategies are not topics in English instruction, nor used in English language training, even though preliminary applications and didactical concepts exist. In light of this, the question arises, which strategies German learners of English use to recode English words. It is not clear whether they continue using the strategy they used for German - serial recoding - or if they learn new strategies, such as recoding using analogies or using the consonants for orientation. These questions are explored in two studies. The first study focuses on recoding according to the grain-size-theory, the second study tests the two-cycles-model with German learners of English. For this purpose, students of grades 5, 7 and 9 of a Gymnasium (Grammar school) and students of a university were asked to read English and German pseudowords and words. The recoding strategies were identified based on reading speed and accuracy. According to the grain-size-theory, switching costs when reading pseudowords with and without orthographic neighbours in mixed lists (compared to blocked lists), should emerge when readers switch between recoding strategies. The word-length-effect, which occurs with serial recoding, can also be used as an indicator for the recoding strategy being employed. Results show that more experienced German learners of English take into account larger units when reading English pseudowords than less experienced learners (the word-length-effect is reduced with more experience) whereas small units were used to recode German pseudowords (word-length-effect is not affected by experience level). Switching costs are not reduced with higher experience levels as expected, but students in grades 7 and 9 grade read pseudowords more easily both with, and without, orthographic neighbours, when they are presented in mixed lists rather than in blocked lists. These results suggest, that students with little experience in English learned to recode using analogies, but initially had difficulties in choosing the relevant strategy and suppressing the other one. This ability emerges with more experience in English. The two-cycles-model was tested using a priming-paradigma. If consonants are processed first and faster than vowels, rapidly presented information about the consonants in target words should facilitate reading. Primes with the same vowels as the target should only facilitate reading when presented for a relatively long period. Accordi g to the results of this study, German learners of English do not process consonants and vowels in different cycles. The results suggest that in a first step the graphemes are translated into German phonemes - in general only the consonants of these phonemes can be used for the English pronunciation. Consequently, the didactics of English as a second language (for German learners), should to take into account the prior knowledge about reading in German, and use it as basis for teaching recoding strategies in English. Teachers of English as a second language should be made aware of these different recoding strategies in German and English. In zwei Studien wird der Frage nachgegangen, welche Strategien deutsche Englischlernerinnen und -lerner beim Rekodieren englischer Wörter verwenden. Unklar ist, ob sie das ihnen aus dem Deutschen bekannte serielle Rekodieren beibehalten oder ob sie zusätzliche Strategien, etwa das Rekodieren mit Hilfe von Analogien oder die besondere Berücksichtigung der Konsonantenstruktur, lernen. In Studie 1 steht das Rekodieren nach der "grain-size"-Theorie im Vordergrund, während in der zweiten Studie das Zwei-Zyklen-Modell überprüft wird. Hierzu wurden 58 Schülerinnen und Schüler der 5., 7. und 9. Klasse eines Gymnasiums sowie 50 Studierende gebeten, englische und deutsche Pseudowörter und Wörter zu lesen. Lesegeschwindigkeit und -genauigkeit dienten als Grundlage für die Bestimmung der Rekodierstrategie. Nach der grain-size-Theorie sollten sich die verwendeten Rekodierstrategien in den Wechselkosten beim Lesen von Pseudowörtern mit und ohne orthographische Nachbarn, die entweder gemischt oder blockweise dargeboten werden, zeigen. Auch der Wortlängeneffekt kann als Hinweis für die verwendete Rekodierstrategie gelten - er entsteht bei seriellem Rekodieren. Es zeigte sich, dass die Studienteilnehmer mit zunehmender Expertise im Englischen größere Einheiten berücksichtigen (der Wortlängeneffekt wird geringer), während sie im Deutschen weiterhin kleine Einheiten zum Rekodieren heranziehen (der Wortlängeneffekt bleibt bestehen). Die Wechselkosten werden im Englischen nicht wie erwartet mit zunehmender Expertise größer, vielmehr fällt es den Jugendlichen der 7. und 9. Klasse leichter, wenn die Pseudowörter mit und ohne orthographische Nachbarn gemischt anstatt blockweise dargeboten werden. Dies lässt vermuten, dass Jugendliche, wenn sie das Rekodieren mit Hilfe von Analogien im Englischen kennen gelernt haben, anfangs Schwierigkeiten haben, die zielführende Rekodierstrategie auszuwählen und die jeweils andere auszublenden. Dies wird erst mit einem gewissen Maß an Expertise möglich. Das Zwei-Zyklen-Modell wurde mit Hilfe eines Priming-Paradigmas (direkt im Anschluss an das erste Experiment) überprüft. Sollte in einem ersten Schritt ein Konsonantengerüst entstehen, müssten kurzzeitig dargebotene Informationen über die im Zielwort enthaltenen Konsonanten das Rekodieren des Zielwortes erleichtern. Vokalgleiche Primes sollten nur bei relativ langer Darbietung des Primes das Rekodieren des Zielwortes vereinfachen. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass deutsche Englischlerner/-innen nicht in zwei getrennt voneinander ablaufenden Zyklen rekodieren. Vielmehr scheint in einem ersten Schritt eine deutsche Phonemfolge zu entstehen, von der im Normalfall nur die Konsonanten für die englische Aussprache verwendet werden können. Für die Englischdidaktik bedeuten die Ergebnisse, dass das Vorwissen aus dem Deutschen nicht ausgeblendet werden kann, sondern dass es als Grundlage für die Vermittlung der Rekodierstrategien verwendet werden sollte. Ausgehend von diesem Vorwissen könnten Rekodierstrategien im Deutschen und Englischen bewusst gemacht werden.
author: Treutlein, Anke

title: Evoking knowledge and information awareness for enhancing computer-supported collaborative problem solving
abstract: Investigated whether computer-supported collaborative problem solving by spatially distributed group members can be fostered by evoking knowledge and information awareness; specifically, awareness of a group member with regard to both their fellow collaborators' domain knowledge and information underlying this knowledge. 90 participants (mean age 24 years) were placed into 30 groups of 3 (triads) resulting in 15 control groups and 15 experimental groups. The triads were required to work in a synchronous fashion in Web-based, shared and unshared desktop working windows. Results confirmed the efficiency of this approach by comparing both an experimental condition in which an environment for fostering knowledge and information awareness was provided as well as in a control condition without such an environment. With regard to communication and cooperation aspects, the quality of the group maps needed for solving the problems and the problem-solving performance was also proved efficient.
author: Engelmann, Tanja; Tergan, Sigmar-Olaf; Hesse, Friedrich W.

title: Peer-Learning als Unterstützungs- und Bildungsangebot im Bachelorstudiengang - Entwicklung und erste Erfahrung mit einem strukturierten Mentorenprogramm
abstract: Im Rahmen der Umstellung von Diplom- auf Bachelorstudiengänge und den damit einhergehenden didaktischen Anforderungen wurde im Sommer 2007 am Psychologischen Institut der Universität Heidelberg eine Zukunftswerkstatt initiiert. Dabei wurden Ideen für eine verbesserte Lehre in den Bachelorstudiengängen entwickelt und als eine konkrete Umsetzung der Aufbau eines strukturierten Peer-Learning-Programms (Comenius-Programm) beschlossen. Den Kern des seit dem Sommersemester 2008 laufenden Programms bildet die Betreuung von Erst- und Zweitsemesterstudierenden durch Studierende höherer Semester (Mentorinnen und Mentoren). Organisatorisch erfolgt die Betreuung und Begleitung in regelmäßigen Kleingruppentreffen und ergänzenden Ein-Tages-Workshops. Inhaltlich stehen die Themen Moderieren und Präsentieren, "Lernen lernen", Zeit- und Stressmanagement, wissenschaftliches Schreiben, kritisches Denken und Vernetzung psychologischer Teilgebiete im Mittelpunkt. Diese Themenauswahl hat die Entwicklung von Kernkompetenzen zum Ziel, die im Studienangebot bisher nicht ausreichend angebahnt wurde. Erste Evaluationsergebnisse zeigen, dass sich die Gestaltung der Lehrveranstaltungen durch das Programm bedeutsam verbessert hat und dass die Mentorinnen und Mentoren als wichtige Unterstützung bei der Bewältigung der gestiegenen Studien- und Lebensanforderungen wahrgenommen werden.
author: Reuschenbach, Bernd; Monter, Anne; Weick, Julia; Kasprzik, Jenna; Klittich, Christiane; Scheiter, Fabian

title: Der Einfluss von Fachexpertise bei Tutoren und Lernenden beim Problembasierten Lernen
abstract: Die Rolle des fachbezogenen Vorwissens von Lernenden und Tutoren beim Problembasierten Lernen wird thematisiert. Bisherige Feldstudien konnten keine homogene Befundlage zum Einfluss der Fachexpertise von Tutoren zeigen bzw. ergaben, dass Lernende ohne Vorwissen eher von Fachtutoren profitieren. In eigenen Vorarbeiten konnte dies für Anfänger in einem Bereich nachgewiesen werden. Darüber hinaus zeigte sich, dass bei einer nicht-fachlichen tutoriellen Betreuung die Gefahr einer systematischen Überschätzung des eigenen Leistungsstandes drohen kann. In einer weiteren Studie konnte dieser Effekt nicht direkt repliziert werden. Allerdings zeigte sich auch hier, dass Lernende mit geringem Vorwissen in höherem Maße von einer fachlichen tutoriellen Betreuung profitieren als von einer nicht-fachlichen. Auch fortgeschrittene Lernende waren noch vulnerabel für diese Intervention, wenngleich auch in deutlich geringerem Maße. Bei der Einschätzung des eigenen Leistungsstandes zeigte sich ebenfalls, dass Lernende mit geringem Vorwissen anfälliger sind für unterschiedliche Betreuungsstrategien als Lernende mit bereits vorhandenem Vorwissen. Insgesamt stützen diese Befunde aus dem Lernlabor die Erkenntnisse der Feldforschung, dass Lernende mit einem geringen Maß an Vorwissen von einer fachlichen Betreuung profitieren und dass Fortgeschrittene durchaus auch von nicht-fachlichen Tutoren profitieren können.
author: Zumbach, Jörg

title: Das Gruppen-Mindmap als didaktisches Element im Seminar
abstract: Der Nutzen von Gruppen-Mindmaps für Lehr-Lern-Situationen wird beschrieben im Kontext der Seminargestaltung im Fachbereich der Sozialen Arbeit an einer Fachhochschule. Beispiele illustrieren die Verwendung von Gruppen-Mindmaps am Beginn, im Verlauf und zum Abschluss von Lernprozessen. Besonders fokussiert wird ihre methodisch-didaktische Einbettung, und die Möglichkeiten und Grenzen von Mindmaps als Element der Lernzielkontrolle werden diskutiert. Es wird deutlich, dass Gruppen-Mindmaps (wie auch Einzel-Mindmaps) ein integrierendes Medium zwischen den Eigenerfahrungen der Studierenden, einer ergebnisorientierten Kleingruppenarbeit und der Einbindung des aktuellen Teilnehmerwissens bilden können. Offene Fragen für die Nutzung der Mindmap-Methode werden insbesondere im Bereich der (selbstorganisierten) Lernzielkontrolle gesehen.
author: Balz, Hans-Jürgen

title: Konfidenzgewichtete True-False Items in Wissenstests für Psychologie-Lehrveranstaltungen
abstract: Konfidenzgewichtete True-False-Items ermöglichen nicht nur eine ökonomische Wissensüberprüfung in Lehr-Lern-Situationen, sondern auch eine Untersuchung didaktischer Merkmale dieser Situationen hinsichtlich ihres Einflusses auf qualitative Aspekte des Lernprozesses. Es werden zwei Feldstudien vorgestellt, die am Beispiel der Auswirkungen einer erwarteten Leistungsbenotung explorieren, wie sich neben der Testleitung auch das metakognitive Monitoring von Studierenden verändert. Daten wurden an Stichproben von 61 und 62 Studierenden im Rahmen von Psychologie-Lehrveranstaltungen erhoben. Studierende, die eine Benotung erwarteten, verbesserten in beiden Studien im Laufe des Semesters die absolute Genauigkeit ihres Monitoring deutlicher als Studierende, die keine Benotung erwarteten - allerdings auf Kosten eines Anstiegs fälschlicher Sicherheit bei inkorrekten Antworten. Beide Studien veranschaulichen, wie mit Hilfe von konfidenzgewichteten True-False-Items nicht nur Wissen geprüft, sondern auch metakognitive Leistungen erfasst werden kann.
author: Barenberg, Jonathan; Dutke, Stephan

title: Lifelong learning as a goal - Do autonomy and self-regulation in school result in well prepared pupils?
abstract: Examined how the promotion of autonomy and self-regulated performance in classroom instruction impacts students' perceptions/attitudes and their motivation to learn. A total of 2,266 fifth, sixth, and seventh graders, and students from college preparatory schools from a total of 125 classes in 28 Austrian schools participated. Individuals completed questionnaires to assess central features of lifelong learning (LLL): scholastic interest, learning goal orientation, self-efficacy and assessment of learning. Participants were also asked to rate their teachers in terms of encouraging autonomy, self-reflection, and performance in the classroom. Gender, domain, and grade were considered in this multilevel analyses which was conducted using Null, Full, and Slopes as outcomes models. Results demonstrated the importance of the classroom instruction/teaching method as an influencing factor on students' "will and skill to learn" (LLL determinants). Additional results showed a decrease in motivation with increasing grade level. In contrast to other studies, disturbing findings from the current research indicate that gender differences in students persist over time. However, high autonomy in the classroom was associated with the reduction of gender differences. Interventions including systematic teacher training and instructional programs to promote a sense of autonomy and self-regulating behavior in the students is stressed.
author: Lüftenegger, Marko; Schober, Barbara; van de Schoot, Rens; Wagner, Petra; Finsterwald, Monika; Spiel, Christiane

title: Mental contrasting promotes integrative bargaining
abstract: Tested the impact of several self-regulatory strategies on an integrative bargaining task. 174 participants (aged 18-21 years) were randomly assigned to dyads and negotiated over the sale of a car. Before negotiating, participants were prompted to engage in one of three self-regulation strategies based upon the fantasy realization theory (FRT): They were to either mentally contrast a successful future agreement with the reality of bargaining, to exclusively elaborate on successful future agreement, or to exclusively elaborate on the reality of bargaining. Those in the control condition merely began the negotiation. Findings reveal that mentally contrasting a successful future agreement with the reality of bargaining led dyads to reach the largest and most equitable joint agreements, compared to dyads that elaborated only on successful future agreement, or on the reality of bargaining. As it was found that mental contrasting promotes integrative agreement, the authors suggest that it is important to learn more about the psychological processes that mediate and moderate this effect. Another related line of research could examine the application of the findings to other bargaining scenarios. The authors further suggest that a future line of research should combine mental contrasting with planning strategies. It is concluded that the result that mental contrasting fosters integrative solutions reflects its potential to help negotiators effectively discriminate among feasible and unfeasible components of a multifaceted goal (integrative agreement).
author: Kirk, Dan; Oettingen, Gabriele; Gollwitzer, Peter M.

title: Learners-as-Designers: Wissensräume mit kognitiven Werkzeugen aktiv nutzen und konstruieren
abstract: Lernangebote von hoher Lernqualität sind dadurch gekennzeichnet, dass sie Lernende dazu anregen, in Wissensräumen vertieftes Wissen zu erwerben und dieses effizient in praktisches Handlungswissen umzusetzen. Vor diesem Hintergrund wird diskutiert, wie der didaktisch-methodische Ansatz "Learners-as-Designers" (LaD) genutzt werden kann, eine solche Lernqualität zu erreichen. Es wird gezeigt, wie LaD unter Nutzung computerbasierter Technologien sowohl in der universitären Lehre als auch in der betrieblichen Weiterbildung umgesetzt werden kann, und mit welchen Effekten, aber auch Herausforderungen eine solche Lehr-Lern-Konzeption verbunden ist. Zusammenfassend wird konstatiert, dass mit Aus- und Weiterbildungskonzeptionen auf Basis von LaD ein Mehrwert erreicht wird. In LaD-Konzeptionen verändern sich die traditionellen Rollen der Lernenden und der Dozenten: Lernende können nicht mehr nur als Rezipient didaktisch aufbereiteten Wissens agieren, Dozenten müssen die Rolle eines Trainers, Beraters und Moderators einnehmen. Solche veränderten Rollen werden als Voraussetzung zum Erwerb eines Wissens angesehen, dass in Anwendungssituationen erfolgreich eingesetzt werden kann. Des Weiteren wird betont, dass durch LaD-Konzeptionen nicht nur ein vertiefter, anwendungsorientierter Erwerb von Fachwissen erzielt wird, sondern auch praktisches Handlungswissen zur strukturierten Aufbereitung und Präsentation von Informationen in Medien vermittelt wird. Wird LaD als Blended-Learning-Arrangement gestaltet, werden Dozenten in die Lage versetzt, sowohl die einzelnen computergestützten Aktivitäten als auch die inhaltliche Arbeit der Lernenden individuell zu unterstützen. Um die Bewältigung der Anforderungen, die mit der Aufbereitung, Nutzung und Kommunikation von Wissen einhergehen, zu gewährleisten, wird der Einsatz computerbasierter Technologien als kognitive Werkzeuge für wesentlich erachtet; somit kann ein Lernen mit computerbasierten Technologien erfolgen, nicht nur ein Lernen von digitalen Medien.
author: Proske, Antje; Damnik, Gregor; Körndle, Hermann

title: Talent development and excellence
abstract: Highlights recent theoretical approaches to talent development and gifted education, and discusses empirical research conclusions deserving more attention. Furthermore, possibilities for harnessing these insights for current talent development and gifted education efforts are considered. - Contents: (A) A systemic theory of giftedness. (1) B. author: Stoeger, Heidrun; Aljughaiman, Abdullah; Harder, Bettina

title: Geschlechtsunterschiede in Motivation und Strategiesystematik beim selbstregulierten Erlernen eines Computerprogramms
abstract: Es wird untersucht, ob Geschlechtsdifferenzen in der Performanz am Computer prozessnah auf Unterschiede in Motivation und Explorationsstrategien zurückgeführt werden können. Forschungsfrage 1 richtete sich auf die reliable und valide Erfassung der Explorationsstrategien beim selbstregulierten Erlernen eines Computerprogramms. Forschungsfrage 2 betraf die Frage, inwiefern Geschlechtsunterschiede in der Leistung auf Variablen des kognitiv-motivationalen Prozessmodells (z. B. Strategiesystematik, Flow-Erleben) zurückgeführt werden können. Der Fokus von Forschungsfrage 3 lag auf der wechselseitigen Beziehung der motivationalen und kognitiven Variablen während des Lernprozesses sowie auf deren Beziehung zur Leistung. Im Rahmen von Forschungsfrage 4 wurde erforscht, ob sich Personen danach klassifizieren lassen, welche Explorationsstrategien sie nutzen und ob sich Männer und Frauen im Muster der Strategienutzung unterscheiden. Insgesamt wurden drei empirische Studien durchgeführt, an denen Studierende der Wirtschaftswissenschaften sowie der Psychologie teilnahmen (Studie 1: N = 18; Studie 2: N = 33; Studie 3: N = 92). Es gelangm ein reliables und valides Messinstrument zur Erfassung der Explorationsstrategien zu entwickeln (die systematische, die rigide Explorationsstrategie sowie die Explorationsstrategie Informationssuche). Eine erste Validierung des Messinstruments zeigte, dass die systematische Explorationsstrategie positiv mit der Leistung und dem Flow-Erleben korrelierte. Die rigide Exploration und die Informationssuche standen dagegen in negativem Zusammenhang mit diesen Außenkriterien. Die Explorationsstrategie Versuch-und-Irrtum wies keine bzw. leicht negative Beziehungen zu den genannten Außenkriterien auf. In Studie 2 zeigten Männer erwartungsgemäß höhere Leistungen, eine höhere aktuelle Motivation und eine günstigere Strategiesystematik. Demgegenüber wurden diese Differenzen in Studie 3 nicht statistisch signifikant. In Studie 2 und 3 fanden sich keine Geschlechtsunterschiede in der Eingangsmotivation. Unterschiede im Flow-Erleben wurden ebenfalls nicht signifikant. In der Computerbildung, welche zur Kontrolle mit erfasst wurde, zeigten Frauen jedoch in beiden Studien eine geringere Computererfahrung. Das Flow-Erleben leistete einen inkrementellen Beitrag zur Erklärung der Leistung. In einer Clusteranalyse konnten drei Personengruppen voneinander abgegrenzt werden. Die erste Gruppe ("Systematische Explorierer") war gekennzeichnet durch eine häufige Nutzung der systematischen Explorationsstrategie. Die zweite Gruppe ("Unsystematische Explorierer") nutzte überwiegend die rigide Explorationsstrategie und die Explorationsstrategie Versuch-und-Irrtum. Bei der dritten Gruppe stand die Informationssuche im Vordergrund. Wurde neben der systematischen und der rigiden Exploration vorwiegend auf die Informationssuche zurückgegriffen, wirkte sich diese Kombination ungünstig auf die Leistung aus, nicht jedoch auf das Flow-Erleben. Die günstigste Motivation und die höchste Leistung erzielten erwartungsgemäß die systematischen Explorierer". Im Unterschied dazu waren die "unsystematischen Explorierer" statistisch signifikant geringer motiviert und waren bei der Aufgabenlösung weniger erfolgreich. Die als unsystematisch eingestuften Explorationsstrategien (Informationssuche, rigide Exploration, Versuch-und-Irrtum) hatten damit unterschiedliche Effekte auf die Motivation und auf die Leistung.
author: Beierlein, Constanze

title: The relevance of physiological activation in experimentally inducing fear, worrying and negative metabeliefs about worrying: Two studies on etiological factors in generalized anxiety disorder
abstract: Investigated etiological factors in the etiology of generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) and the relevance of physiological activation in its maintenance. After a survey of etiological models of GAD and the related empirical research, a new integrative model of GAD incorporating current and overlapping conceptualizations is presented, which focuses on the role of physiological activation in the maintenance of the disorder. Using an experimental method for inducing activation by carbon dioxide-enriched air, two studies were conducted to investigate the role of different maintaining factors for GAD symptoms. In a sample of 60 undergraduate students (mean age 21 years), Study 1 examined whether imagining a personally relevant feared future outcome triggers worrying and negative metabeliefs about worrying, particularly when fear imagery is accompanied by physiological activation. In addition to 32 control subjects, 28 subjects were GAD analog participants who habitually engage in excessive worrying. Results showed that GAD analogs had more fear, worried more, had more negative metabeliefs about worry after imagining the feared future outcome. However, physiological activation increased only metacognitions in GAD analogs. Study 2 involved 41 healthy undergraduates (mean age 21 years) who did not display excessive worrying. It focused on the effects of the interaction of physiological arousal and its interpretation on the maintaining factors anxiety, worry, and metaworries. False feedback concerning the perceived physiological activation as overactivation led to the maintenance of fear, worry, and negative metacognitions. Therefore, misinterpretation of physiological activation is considered a premorbid marker of GAD. Implications for GAD treatment and further studies are discussed.
author: Patzelt, Julia

title: Sleep timing is more important than sleep length or quality for medical school performance (PSYNDEXshort)
abstract: Overwhelming evidence supports the importance of sleep for memory consolidation. Medical students are often deprived of sufficient sleep due to large amounts of clinical duties and university load, we therefore investigated how study and sleep habits influence university performance. We performed a questionnaire-based study with 31 medical students of the University of Munich (second and third clinical semesters; surgery and internal medicine). The students kept a diary (in 30-min bins) on their daily schedules (times when they studied by themselves, attended classes, slept, worked on their thesis, or worked to earn money). The project design involved three 2-wk periods (A: during the semester; B: directly before the exam period - pre-exam; C: during the subsequent semester break). Besides the diaries, students completed once questionnaires about their sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index [PSQI]), their chronotype (Munich Chronotype Questionnaire [MCTQ]), and their academic history (previous grades, including the previously achieved preclinical board exam [PBE]). Analysis revealed significant correlations between the actual sleep behavior during the semester (MSdiary; mid-sleep point averaged from the sleep diaries) during the pre-exam period and the achieved grade (p = 0.002) as well as between the grades of the currently taken exam and the PBE (p = 0.002). A regression analysis with MSdiary pre-exam and PBE as predictors in a model explained 42.7% of the variance of the exam grade (effect size 0.745). Interestingly, MSdiary - especially during the pre-exam period - was the strongest predictor for the currently achieved grade, along with the preclinical board exam as a covariate, whereas the chronotype did not significantly influence the exam grade. author: Genzel, L.; Ahrberg, K.; Roselli, C.; Niedermaier, S.; Steiger, A.; Dresler, M.; Roenneberg, T.

title: AD(H)S - Hilfe zur Selbsthilfe : Lern- und Verhaltensstrategien für Schule, Studium und Beruf
abstract: Das Buch vermittelt nützliche und erprobte Strategien, wie Menschen, die von AD(H)S, der Aufmerksamkeitsdefizit-(Hyperaktivitäts-)Störung, betroffen sind, durch Selbstmanagement ihr Leistungsvermögen und ihr Sozialverhalten verbessern können. - Inhalt: (1) Anders sein und viele Fähigkeiten haben: das ist AD(H)S. (2) Nur wenn ich weiß, warum ich so bin, kann ich bewusst etwas dagegen tun. (3) Sport und Bewegung: wichtige Bestandteile jeder AD(H)S-Therapie. (4) Erfolgreich lernen und studieren, den Lernprozess automatisieren. (5) Selbstwertgefühl und soziale Kompetenz auf Dauer verbessern. (6) Konkrete Strategien zur Verbesserung von Leistung und Verhalten. (7) Besonderheiten bei der Behandlung von Jugendlichen. (8) Erwachsen mit AD(H)S. (9) AD(H)S bedeutete Stress von Anfang an. (10) Versagen trotz sehr guter Intelligenz. (11) Strategien zur Diagnostik und Behandlung von AD(H)S-bedingter Leserechtschreib- und Rechenschwäche. (12) Fernsehen, Computerspiele und AD(H)S. (13) Wie kann die Schule bei AD(H)S unterstützen und fördern? (14) Die Wirkungsweise der Medikamente und was man darüber wissen sollte. (15) Wie die wichtigsten Therapiefehler vermieden werden. (16) Leistungsstark, selbstbewusst und psychisch stabil: therapeutische Strategien und ein gute Selbstmanagement machen es möglich.
author: Simchen, Helga

title: Confusion can be beneficial for learning
abstract: Examined the role of confusion in fostering deep learning and critical thinking. In Experiment 1, confusion was induced via a contradictory information manipulation. 63 college students (aged 18-50 years) engaged in multiturn trialogues with two animated conversational agents and attempted to detect flaws in sample research studies. Experiment 2 (76 college students aged 18-45 years) had a delayed contradiction manipulation to induce confusion, where the agents initially agreed with each other, but eventually started to express divergent views. Short explanatory reading texts were also provided as an intervention to potentially alleviate confusion. Learners' confusion levels were measured via retrospective affect judgment (Experiment 1) and online self-report (Experiment 2) along with accuracy of responses to forced-choice questions immediately following contradictory statements (both experiments). Learning was measured with multiple-choice posttests that assessed shallow knowledge of scientific reasoning concepts (both experiments) and with near and far transfer versions of a flaw detection task (Experiment 2). Results showed that learners who were confused by the contradictions were significantly more accurate at detecting flaws in transfer case studies than those in the control condition without contradictions. Overall results indicate that confusion can be effective in complex learning activities and that there might be some benefits to designing educational interventions that intentionally perplex learners.
author: D'Mello, Sidney; Lehman, Blair; Pekrun, Reinhard; Graesser, Art

title: Fostering multiple text comprehension: How metacognitive strategies and motivation moderate the text-belief consistency effect
abstract: Examined the effectiveness of information of three metacognitive strategies tailored to strengthen the comprehension of belief-inconsistent information during multiple text comprehension. According to theories of self-regulated learning, knowledge about relevant metacognitive strategies improves comprehension only when learners are also motivated to use these strategies. These hypotheses were investigated in an experiment in which 85 college students (mean age 24 years) read one belief-consistent and one belief-inconsistent text about a controversial scientific issue. Participants either received information about three metacognitive strategies or no additional information. Moreover, participants' motivation was manipulated by providing them with either negative or positive performance feedback or no feedback. Results are in line with predictions and show a text-belief consistency effect, which was eliminated by strengthening the situation model for the belief-inconsistent text only when learners received information about relevant metacognitive strategies and were motivated to use these strategies after positive performance feedback. It is concluded that the text-belief consistency effect can be overcome through the use of metacognitive strategies, as long as readers are motivated to accept challenges to their prior beliefs.
author: Maier, Johanna; Richter, Tobias

title: Studienzufriedenheit und psychische Belastungen von Medizinstudierenden : Ein Vergleich zwischen Studierenden in München und Witten/Herdecke
abstract: Ziel dieser Studie ist es, Einflussfaktoren auf die Studien- und Lebenszufriedenheit, die gesundheitsbezogene Lebensqualität und die psychische Gesundheit von Medizinstudierenden genauer zu beleuchten. Zu diesem Zweck wurden 76 Medizinstudierende der Universität Witten/Herdecke und 343 Medizinstudierende der Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München mittels einer Online-Fragebogenbatterie, bestehend aus den etablierten Selbstbeurteilungsinstrumenten SWE, ADS-K, PSQ, SF-12 und STQL-S, befragt . Die Studierenden beider Universitäten zeigen sich deutlich belasteter als die gleichaltrige Allgemeinbevölkerung. Defizite ergeben sich sowohl für die gesundheitsbezogene Lebensqualität als auch für die psychische Gesundheit und im Gesundheitsverhalten. Für die Studierenden, die in Witten/Herdecke nach einem Reformstudiengang lernen ergeben sich signifikant bessere Werte bezüglich Stressbelastung, Depressivität, Zufriedenheit und Selbstwirksamkeitserwartung, trotz ähnlicher Arbeitsbelastung sowie vergleichbaren Stressbewältigungs- und Coping-Strategien, Die Zufriedenheit mit dem Studium scheint größtenteils durch die subjektive Belastung und die psychische Gesundheit, aber auch durch die Wohnsituation der Studierenden und die Form des Curriculums beeinflusst zu sein. Die vorliegende Studie bestätigt den hohen Bedarf an weiteren Reformen der medizinischen Ausbildung und umfangreichen Präventionsangeboten von Seiten der Hochschulen. Eine systematische Aufklärung über Stressoren und Risikofaktoren im Studium und späteren Berufsleben, innovative Lehrkonzepte über gesundheitsförderndes Verhalten, spezielle Kurse zu Stressbewältigung und Lernstrategien im Medizinstudium und das Angebot niederschwelliger Beratungsangebote könnten die Studienzufriedenheit und somit auch die Lebensqualität der angehenden Medizinerinnen und Mediziner deutlich erhöhen.
author: Ulrich, Christina

title: Prediction of attendance at fitness center: A comparison between the theory of planned behavior, the social cognitive theory, and the physical activity maintenance theory
abstract: Examined predictions of attendance behavior at fitness centers, comparing the physical-activity maintenance theory (PAMT), the theory of planned behavior (TPB), and social-cognitive theory (SCT). In the processes of physical activity (PA) maintenance-specific predictors are effective, which differ from other stages of PA development. Recently, PAMT was specifically developed for prediction of PA maintenance. Participation rate in a fitness center was observed for 101 college students (53 female, mean age 23 years) over 20 weeks using a magnetic card. Participants completed the Recent Life Changes Questionnaire, and a series of questionnaires on self-efficacy, outcome expectancies, environmental barriers (impediments), social support, personal goals, and self-motivation. Results of a latent class zero-inflated Poisson growth curve analysis identified two participation patterns: regular attenders and intermittent exercisers. SCT showed the highest predictive power followed by PAMT and TPB. Impeding aspects such as life stress and barriers were the strongest predictors, suggesting that overcoming barriers might be an important aspect for working out on a regular basis. Self-efficacy, perceived behavioral control, and social support could also significantly differentiate between the participation patterns.
author: Jekauc, Darko; Völkle, Manuel; Wagner, Matthias O.; Mess, Filip; Reiner, Miriam; Renner, Britta

title: Cross-country generalizability of the role of metacognitive knowledge in students' strategy use and reading competence (PSYNDEXshort)
abstract: Background/Context: Because metacognitive knowledge includes knowledge about adequate learning strategies, and because an effective use of learning strategies is associated with higher levels of performance, substantial relationships can be assumed between metacognitive knowledge, strategic behavior, and performance. However, such a pattern of results is rarely found in the research literature. In part, this may be due to inadequate indicators of strategy use. Purpose of study: Prior research showed that high scores on self-reported strategy use were only mirrored in high levels of performance when students had sufficient metacognitive knowledge. To test the cross-country generalizability of the relationship between metacognitive knowledge, strategy use, and reading competence, we analyzed data from the PISA 2009-study, in which similar measures of metacognitive knowledge as well as of students' strategy use were used. Research Design: The study uses a cross-sectional correlational design. It draws on representative samples of fifteen-year-old students from 34 OECD countries taking part in the PISA 2009 study. The relations between students' reading competence scores, their metacognitive knowledge as well as their self-reported use of learning strategies were analyzed. We used correlations, mediation, as well as moderator regression analyses to predict students' reading competence. Findings/Results: Results showed consistently moderate to high correlations between metacognitive knowledge and reading competence. There were also lower, but still significant, relationships between strategy use and both reading competence and metacognitive knowledge. Testing a "mediator model" with strategy use as a mediator resulted in small but significant effects of strategy use as mediator. Assuming that metacognitive knowledge might be a necessary precondition for effective strategy use, the study tested whether it served as a moderator. Results confirmed this moderator effect for many but not all countries. However, across all countries, there was a consistently high effect of metacognitive knowledge on reading competence, independent of the level of self-reported use of strategies. Conclusions/Recommendations: The results are very similar across countries. Taken together, the findings suggest that metacognitive knowledge as measured by a test tapping declarative, conditional and relational strategy knowledge is an important predictor of students' reading competence, and contributes significantly to our understanding of what helps students to become better readers. Metacognitive knowledge captures the prerequisite of adaptive strategic processing of texts. Increasing students' knowledge in this domain is a promising approach when it comes to fostering self-regulated reading.
author: Artelt, Cordula; Schneider, Wolfgang

title: Will you thrive under pressure or burn out? Linking anxiety motivation and emotional exhaustion
abstract: Examined the effects of using anxiety as a source of energy or as a source of information (viewed here as two forms of anxiety motivation) on emotional exhaustion. It was of interest whether individual differences in the tendency to use anxiety as a source of motivation can explain emotional exhaustion. Moreover, the moderating role of trait anxiety was assessed. Results show that in Study 1, with 86 participants, the use of anxiety as a source of energy predicted decreased emotional exhaustion in teachers and medical doctors (mean age 44 years) one year later. Moreover, both forms of anxiety motivation buffered individuals from the detrimental effects of trait anxiety (State-Trait Anxiety Inventory, STAI) on later emotional exhaustion (Maslach Burnout Inventory - General Survey, MBI-GS). In Study 2, an experiment, 91 participants (college students with a mean age of 22 years) who were instructed to use anxiety as a source of energy reported lower emotional exhaustion (MBI-GS) following a stressful task (a subset of Raven's Standard Progressive Matrices, SPM, under exaggerated time pressure), compared to those instructed to focus on the task or to simply do their best. It is concluded that using anxiety as a source of motivation may protect people against emotional exhaustion.
author: Strack, Juliane; Lopes, Paulo N.; Esteves, Francisco

title: Watching corresponding gestures facilitates learning with animations by activating human mirror-neurons: An fNIRS study
abstract: Tested whether viewing corresponding gestures performed by others is helpful for learning about nonhuman movement during dynamic visualizations. The study examined whether these gestures activate cortical areas related to the human mirror-neuron system (hMNS) by triggering anthropomorphized encoding, a mapping between the to-be-learned contents and body-based representations. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) was employed to assess cortical activation while 45 college students (mean age 24 years) learned how to classify different fish according to their movement patterns based on animated videos along with video depictions of an expert performing a corresponding gesture (and noncorresponding gesture). Measures included a questionnaire assessing students' familiarity with the domain, a short version of the paper folding test (PFT), and a movement pattern classification test. Results confirmed that viewing corresponding gestures activated areas related to the hMNS particularly for low-visuospatial ability learners. Gesture-based interventions may help to stimulate more efficient processing of dynamic visualizations for this group of individuals. Follow up-studies to directly assess whether the corresponding gestures fostered learning or not as compared to a no-gesture-condition, and to investigate the effectiveness of dynamic visualizations and their ability to activate brain areas related to the hMNS are recommended.
author: Brucker, Birgit; Ehlis, Ann-Christine; Häußinger, Florian B.; Fallgatter, Andreas J.; Gerjets, Peter

title: Action control bridges the planning-behaviour gap: A longitudinal study on physical exercise in young adults
abstract: Objectives: Maintaining physical exercise levels may not only require motivation and planning but also action control which is supposed to mediate between planning and exercise. Design: Behavioral intention, action planning, coping planning and past behavior were assessed at baseline, and action control and concurrent exercise were measured one month later in 497 young adults. Method: Three nested structural models were specified to examine different mediation mechanisms. One model reflected the intention-planning-behavior chain, the other one focused on the intention-action control-behavior chain and the third model comprised the full sequence. Results: Indirect effects from intentions on exercise involved either planning or action control as mediating variables. In Model 3, all three constructs (action planning, coping planning and action control) were sequential mediators between intentions and later physical exercise levels. Action and coping planning were not directly but indirectly related to exercise via action control. Conclusions: Findings support the sequential mediation for planning and action control as antecedents of physical exercise. Action control is needed for exercise, because planning in itself is not always sufficient. Maintaining exercise levels may be attributed to effective self-regulatory strategies such as action control in combination with planning.
author: Reyes Fernández, Benjamin; Fleig, Lena; Godinho, Cristina A.; Montenegro Montenegro, Esteban; Knoll, Nina; Schwarzer, Ralf

title: Studying against your will: Motivational interference in action
abstract: Examined motivational conflicts and specific difficulties in self-regulated learning during daily studying activities. During an experience-sampling period of 7 days, 58 college students (mean age 24 years) used smartphones to record information on their daily activities, motivational conflicts, and momentary affect. Measures included the Short Scale of Positive and Negative Affect and Valence (PANAVA) and the Student Adaptation to College Questionnaires (SACQ). The Rubicon model of action phases provided an integrative framework of motivation, breaking down goal-directed behavior into action phases and delineating motivational and volitional processes. Results revealed that motivational conflict during studying is a frequent occurrence and most students struggle with it. Volitional strategies and interventions that foster students' capacities for self-control may not necessarily solve these self-regulation problems which are motivational in nature. Alternatively, setting and initiating goals that provide positive affect, and provide students with the opportunity to discover their true interests (identify implicit preferences) is the primary task for parents and educators.
author: Grund, Axel; Schmid, Sebastian; Fries, Stefan

title: Completion problems can reduce the illusions of understanding in a computer-based learning environment on genetics
abstract: Examined the influence of different types of instructional support (incomplete worked-out examples vs completion problems and conventional problems) on metacognitive judgments of task difficulty and invested mental effort. 67 college students (mean age 22 years) solved five training problems on the subject of genetic inheritance followed by a post-test. All material, including a prior knowledge test, a perceived difficulty scale, and a mental effort rating scale were presented in a Web-based learning environment. Results indicate that irrespective of the type of instructional support, students increased their performance significantly from prior knowledge test to posttest. As predicted, students learning with incomplete worked-out examples showed an underestimation of task difficulty and overestimated their performance compared with students from the other two conditions. Contrary to the hypothesis, accuracy of metacognitive judgments was not influenced by students' prior knowledge. In sum, incomplete worked-out examples are prone to trigger an illusion of understanding. Further research to examine effects from the use of completion problems for learning tasks of different complexities is suggested.
author: Mihalca, Loredana; Mengelkamp, Christoph; Schnotz, Wolfgang; Paas, Fred

title: Epistemological beliefs and students' adaptive perception of task complexity
abstract: Investigated students' epistemological beliefs and adaptive perception of task complexity. A total sample of 102 college students initially completed the Epistemological Beliefs Inventory (EBI) and the Connotative Aspects of Epistemological Beliefs (CAEB) questionnaires online. In subsequent small group sessions, subjects then completed a knowledge test about a chosen topic and received additional factual information about it. Subjects then evaluated six learning tasks of different complexities with the COPES questionnaire based on the COPES model of conditions, operations, products, evaluations, and standards. Results demonstrated that students were able to successfully monitor tasks with regard to complexity, and showed adequate knowledge of the task definitions, goals, and plans necessary for learning.
author: Bromme, Rainer; Stahl, Elmar; Pieschl, Stephanie

title: Effects of additional yoga, meditation and homework: A randomized controlled trial evaluating sleep problems with a university student sample (PSYNDEXshort)
abstract: Aims: To investigate the effects of a theory-based treatment (active control condition) addressing social-cognitive constructs on healthy lifestyle behaviors, and whether additional effects would occur if additional practical exercises with yoga, meditation, and homework to improve self-regulatory strategies (intervention condition) were added. Study Design: Pilot study. Place and Duration: An international university in Germany, four weeks. Methodology: 23 undergraduate students were allocated either to an active control group (sessions addressing social-cognitive constructs, with no yoga, meditation, or homework) or an intervention group (sessions addressing social-cognitive constructs, with additional practical exercise in yoga and meditation, and homework to increase self-regulation). Students participated in weekly sessions over four weeks. All study participants improved in their self-regulatory skills (pros, subjective norm, self-efficacy, goal setting and cons). Effects on sleep problems transpired as an interaction of time and treatment group (Eta²=.13). The intervention increased self-regulatory strategies more than the active control treatment (Eta²=.17). Conclusion: Results highlight the importance of exercising yoga and meditation, and providing additional material to enhance self-regulatory strategies. By doing so, sleep problems in students can be reduced.
author: Whittal, Amanda; Wienert, Julian; Lippke, Sonia

title: The impact of cross-curricular competences and prior knowledge on learning outcomes (PSYNDEXshort)
abstract: This review begins by outlining the historical discussion about the relative importance of fostering cross-curricular competencies versus domain-specific prior knowledge as central goals of education. Metacognition and prior knowledge are then introduced as constructs representing these two goals; their development and effects on learning outcomes are described from a theoretical perspective. Empirical research on metacognition and expertise - and especially on mechanisms of acquisition is then presented, illustrating commonalities between the two concepts and drawing attention to the need to take interactions between the two into account when analyzing their impact on learning outcomes. Most of the research discussed in the article draws on cross-sectional data. Systematic longitudinal research of combined effects in different subject domains is required to gain a better understanding of developmental mechanisms and stage-specific effects.
author: Neuenhaus, Nora; Artelt, Cordula; Schneider, Wolfgang

title: Not everybody needs help to seek help: Surprising effects of metacognitive instructions to foster help-seeking in an online-learning environment (PSYNDEXshort)
abstract: Offering help functions is a standard feature of computer-based interactive learning environments (ILE). Nevertheless, a number of recent studies indicate that learners are not using such help facilities effectively. We compared the effects of different metacognitive supports to foster learners' help-seeking behavior in an ILE for plant identification. Four groups of university students (n = 51), each receiving a different metacognitive instruction, had to determine living plants. They had to think-aloud and were video recorded during the experiment. At the end of the session they completed a knowledge test. The surprising effect was that students in all groups were effective help-seekers. They adapted their help-seeking behavior to the complexity of the plants in an effective way. The results indicate that for students on university level effective help-seeking seems to depend largely on motivational factors.
author: Stahl, Elmar; Bromme, Rainer

title: Promoting action control and coping planning to improve hand hygiene
abstract: Examined a brief educational intervention addressing hand hygiene self-regulatory mechanisms, and evaluated which psychological mechanisms may lead to hand hygiene behaviors. 242 students (mean age 21 years) received either an experimental (n = 149) or a control condition on action control and planning (n = 93). Hand hygiene, coping planning, and action control were measured at baseline and six weeks later. The experimental condition addressing planning to perform hand hygiene was compared with a control condition, and working mechanisms were evaluated. Results show that the intervention had an effect on action control, as reflected by a time by treatment interaction. The direct effect of the intervention on behavior was, however, nonsignificant. Changes in action control led to changes in coping planning. These social-cognitive changes mediated the effect of intervention on behavior, after controlling for gender, baseline behavior, and classroom membership. It is concluded that in spite of the associations between the intervention and self-regulatory strategies, no direct effect on behavior could be found. The intervention is argued to have led to an improvement of hand hygiene only indirectly via changes in self-regulatory factors.
author: Reyes Fernández, Benjamín; Lippke, Sonia; Knoll, Nina; Blanca Moya, Emanuel; Schwarzer, Ralf

title: A longitudinal study on information-seeking knowledge in psychology undergraduates: Exploring the role of information literacy instruction and working memory capacity
abstract: No longitudinal studies on whether the acquisition information literacy requires formal instruction or whether it just develops "naturally" have yet been published. Moreover, no studies exist on individual and situational factors moderating the long-term development of information literacy. For these reasons, a three-semester long, four-wave longitudinal study on information-seeking knowledge (a major aspect of information literacy) was conducted with 137 psychology undergraduates (first wave). With regard to situational factors, curriculum-embedded information literacy instruction was contrasted with library instruction. Concerning individual factors, the role of working memory capacity was explored on cognitive load theory grounds. Data were analyzed through multi-level modeling. Results revealed a linear increase in information-seeking knowledge across the four waves, which remained significant when controlling for the effects of information literacy instruction. Curriculum-embedded instruction seemed more effective than library instruction. Working memory capacity moderated the development of information-seeking knowledge: Students with a high working memory capacity had steeper learning curves than those with lower working memory capacity. Results were robust when controlling for additional individual factors known to have an impact on knowledge development, namely fluid intelligence, epistemic beliefs, and domain-specific self-efficacy beliefs. We conclude that instruction plays a key role in information literacy development, especially when it is embedded into the respective curriculum. Moreover, reducing cognitive load is crucial for the acquisition of information-seeking knowledge. Efforts should therefore be made to enhance the usability of information search tools and to provide well-structured online tutorials and instructional modules, for example by using authentic, real-world learning tasks.
author: Rosman, Tom; Mayer, Anne-Kathrin; Krampen, Günter

title: Working memory capacity and disfluency effect: An aptitude-treatment-interaction study
abstract: Investigated the aptitude-treatment interaction between working memory capacity and disfluency. A sample of 65 college students with varying degrees of prior knowledge about the presented topic reviewed instructional materials with either an easy to read or difficult font. Learning outcomes, task enjoyment, task interest, and motivation were assessed posttask. Participants also completed a working memory test and a cognitive-load questionnaire. Results revealed significant aptitude-treatment interaction effects with respect to retention and comprehension. Working memory capacity had a significant influence only in the disfluency condition: The higher the working-memory capacity, the better the retention and comprehension performance in the disfluency condition. No effects were found with respect to transfer or cognitive load. Additional research regarding the role of metacognitive regulation and its possible effects on cognitive load is recommended.
author: Lehmann, Janina; Goussios, Christina; Seufert, Tina

title: Need for cognitive closure may impede the effectiveness of epistemic belief instruction
abstract: Examined the effects of the need for cognitive closure on the efficacy of an instruction to enhance epistemic belief. Individual differences in need for closure are assumed to interfere with the mechanisms postulated in L.D. Bendixen's (2002) process model of epistemic change and, thus, impede intervention effectiveness. A short-term epistemic-belief intervention drawing on both the presentation of diverging (i.e., controversial) information and on constructivist teaching approaches (i.e., moderated discussion) was developed. Instruction primarily aimed at reducing absolute and multiplicistic beliefs in psychology freshmen. In a pretest-posttest field-experimental study, 83 psychology freshmen were randomly assigned to the intervention group or one of two control groups (learning strategies instruction group or untreated control group). As expected, the epistemic-belief intervention reduced both absolute and multiplicistic beliefs. With regard to multiplicistic beliefs, a high need for closure significantly reduced instruction efficacy. The findings are concluded to highlight the crucial importance of considering individual differences in epistemic-belief instruction.
author: Rosman, Tom; Mayer, Anne-Kathrin; Peter, Johannes; Krampen, Günter

title: The effectiveness of a multimodal concept of audition training for music students in coping with music performance anxiety
abstract: Music performance anxiety (MPA) occurs regularly before and during a musical stage performance. Coping with MPA optimizes the performance outcome and plays an important role for musicians, especially when auditioning for work in an orchestra. In this study, the effectiveness of a seminar to train students to cope with MPA was evaluated. Thirteen music students participated in the intervention program of 14 weekly sessions. Eight students were in the control group. The intervention contained video feedback, exercises in methods of body awareness, and insights into cognitive strategies. All students were required to perform two simulated auditions, at the beginning and at the end of the semester. They filled in self-assessment questionnaires related to MPA at both auditions. Additionally, two judges rated the performances in both auditions. Audio recordings of the performances were also sent to 12 orchestral musicians for appraisal as well. The results revealed significant improvements in coping with MPA, shown in the participants' self-assessment ratings as well as in the ratings of the judges during the auditions in the trained group compared with the control group. Additionally, the orchestral musicians rated the audio presentations of the intervention group in the second audition significantly better than the control group.
author: Spahn, Claudia; Walther, Julia-Caroline; Nusseck, Manfred

title: Bachelorstudium Musiktherapie nach dem Heidelberger "CORE-Prinzip"
abstract: Der Bachelorstudiengang Musiktherapie nach dem Heidelberger CORE-Prinzip (Competence-Oriented Research and Education) wird vorgestellt. Die Bedeutung von aktivem und eigenverantwortlichem Lernen wird beschrieben und ein Einblick in die wichtigsten Qualitäten des Prinzips gegeben: themenzentrierte Fünf-Wochen-Blöcke, kompetenzorientierte Prüfungsformen, aktivierende Lehr- und Lernmethoden, intensive fachliche und persönliche Betreuung sowie Innovation und Forschung. Abschließend werden erste Erfahrungen mit der Umsetzung reflektiert.
author: Wormit, Alexander F.

title: Effects of informing learners about the dangers of making overconfident judgments of learning
abstract: Examined the effects of informing learners about the dangers of making overconfident judgments of learning. Learners often insufficiently monitor their comprehension, which results in overconfident judgments of learning and underachievement. In the three present experiments, the authors investigated whether insufficient comprehension monitoring is due in part to the fact that learners are not sufficiently aware of the benefit of comprehension monitoring and thus scarcely engage in this process. As an intervention, learners were informed about the likely negative consequences of failing to monitor their comprehension. Specifically, they were informed about the high frequency of and the detrimental consequences that result from making overconfident judgments of learning. Results of Experiment 1 (42 college students mean age 25 years) showed that for university students, this intervention increased their engagement in comprehension monitoring, led to more cautious judgments of learning, and fostered the acquisition of conceptual knowledge in a subsequent learning phase in which they received instructional explanations relating to a new topic. By contrast, this intervention was less beneficial for 74 eighth graders (aged 13- to 15-year-old). Although the intervention increased their comprehension monitoring and led to more cautious judgments of learning, it did not foster the acquisition of conceptual knowledge from the subsequent explanations (Experiment 2). In Experiment 3, the authors varied whether 97 13- to 15-year-old high school students received (a) information about the frequency of and the detrimental consequences that result from making overconfident judgments of learning and (b) information about effective regulation strategies. Results of this experiment suggest that the limited beneficial effect found in Experiment 2 could be attributed to a lack of knowledge regarding effective regulation strategies for this age group.
author: Roelle, Julian; Schmidt, Elisabeth Marie; Buchau, Alica; Berthold, Kirsten

title: Wissenschaftskommunikation und Experten-Laien-Kommunikation: Kompetenzerwerb durch Trainingsseminare an deutschen und georgischen Universitäten
abstract: Die Förderung kommunikativer Kompetenzen für die adressatengerechte Weitergabe fachlicher Inhalte an Experten und Laien wird als eine Aufgabe von Schule, Hochschule, Aus- und Fortbildung thematisiert. Vor diesem Hintergrund werden mehrere Varianten eines Trainingskonzepts vorgestellt, das durch Selbstorganisation, Handlungstraining und Feedback gekennzeichnet ist. Zwei Beispiele werden näher beschrieben und in ihrer Wirksamkeit evaluiert. Es handelt sich dabei um zwei Varianten der Veranstaltung "Kommunikations-, Moderations-, Präsentations- und Arbeitstechniken im selbstorganisierten Studium" (KOMPASS), einerseits ein seitens der Trainingsgruppen selbstständig zu strukturierendes "Selbstorganisiertes Lernen" (SOL), andererseits ein durch Lehrende bzw. Tutoren angeleitetes und strukturiertes "Handlungsorientiertes Training" (HOT) mit selbstorganisiert durchzuführenden Teilaufgaben. Eine Evaluation mit Vorher-Nachher-Vergleich (an der Universität I. Chavchavadze in Tiblis und der Goethe-Universität Frankfurt) ergab für beide Varianten eine Zunahme von Präsentations- und Trainerkompetenzen. Außerdem demonstrierten die Unterschiede zwischen den verschiedenen Seminarformen und zwischen den verschiedenen Trainerkompetenzen in nachvollziehbarer Weise, dass kommunikative Kompetenzbereiche in verschiedenen Trainingsvarianten zu Präsentations- und Trainingskompetenzen gefördert werden, in Abhängigkeit von den Trainingsformen und Inhalten, jedoch in unterschiedlicher Intensität.
author: Preiser, Siegfried; Turashvili, Tamara

title: Konzeption eines PBL-Moduls im Rahmen des Psychologiestudiums
abstract: Ausgehend vom Hinweis auf die hohe Bedeutung von Kompetenzorientierung, Eigenverantwortung und Selbstorganisation im Rahmen eines berufsvorbereitenden Studiums wird das Grundlagenmodul "Differentielle und Persönlichkeitspsychologie" an der Fakultät für Angewandte Psychologie der SRH Hochschule Heidelberg dargestellt, in dem bereits zu Beginn des Studiums ein hohes Maß an selbstgesteuertem, soziokonstruktivistischem Lernen durch "Problembasiertes Lernen" (PBL) stattfindet. Dabei durchlaufen die Studierenden einen selbstorganisierten und -gesteuerten Prozess unter tutorieller Begleitung. Die Curriculumsgestaltung, die Ausbildung der Tutoren und die Ergebnisse der jüngsten studentischen Lehrevaluation werden vorgestellt. Im Bereich der Fallkonstruktion, die für PBL-Tutorien unabdingbar ist, erwiesen sich Inhalte mit größeren Interpretationsmöglichkeiten und Alltagsbezug, gerade im Bachelorstudium, als besonders geeignet, da sie die für den Erkenntnisprozess notwendige Verbindung von Theorie und Praxis begünstigen. Die Integration des PBL-Konzepts in die psychologische Ausbildung an der Fakultät für Angewandte Psychologie hat sich bewährt: Neben der intensiveren Verarbeitungstiefe des Lernstoffes konnten die Studierenden weitere wichtige, berufsbezogene Kompetenzen erwerben, die zu einer Erhöhung der "Employability" führen.
author: Knöpfel, Markus; Musolesi, Frank; Neuthinger, Willi

title: Self-regulated learning from illustrated text: Eye movement modelling to support use and regulation of cognitive processes during learning from multimedia
abstract: Investigated whether the positive effects of eye movement modeling examples (EMME) on self-regulated multimedia learning, previously found in elementary school children, extend to university students and the teaching of more comprehensive processing strategies. Moreover, it was examined whether EMME's effectiveness depends upon a learner's cognitive prerequisites. EMME are prerecorded eye movements of a skilled learner superimposed over the material to show learners how to adequately process multimedia instruction when learning from text and pictures. In a sample of university students with different study majors, different prior knowledge aspects were assessed as cognitive prerequisites. Before learning about mitosis from a multimedia instruction, students either received no intervention or saw EMME demonstrating various multimedia learning processes. Learning outcomes and eye movements served as dependent variables. Results show that learners in the EMME group processed pictures more intensely and displayed more frequent transitions between text and pictures. Weaker learners showed poorer recall performance after having studied EMME, whereas EMME had no effect on stronger students. In a forced-choice verification task, stronger students benefitted from EMME, whereas no effect was found for weaker students. Picture processing time was found to explain the positive effects of EMME for stronger students. It is concluded that EMME, which illustrate a comprehensive set of cognitive processes, support multimedia learning for stronger university students.
author: Scheiter, Katharina; Schubert, Carina; Schüler, Anne

title: Anstelle von studentischer Revolution, Resignation und Vereinsamung - Engagement und "Lebendiges Lernen" : Zur psychosozialen Situation von Studenten und "neue" Kooperationsformen in der Hochschulausbildung
abstract: Bedingungen von Lernhemmungen und psychischen Störungen bei Studenten werden empirisch untersucht. Es wird ein praktisch erprobtes Programm zur Verbesserung von Arbeitstechnik und Kommunikation vorgelegt, dem unter anderem das Konzept der "Themenzentrierten Interaktion" zugrunde liegt. - Aus dem Inhaltsverzeichnis: (A) K.-J. Kluge und P. Roeben: "Bin ich nichts wert?" - Wie erleben Studenten sich selbst und ihre Studiensituation? (1) Bedingungsanalyse und Erfassung psychischer Störungen bei Studenten - eine Literaturanalyse. (2) Psychische Störungen in der Selbsteinschätzung Studierender der Verhaltensauffaelligenpaedagogik an der Abteilung für Heilpädagogik Köln. (3) Die Studiensituation im Lehr- und Forschungsbereich "Verhaltensauffaelligenpaedagogik" an der Universität Köln im Urteil der Studierenden. - (B) K.-J. Kluge und J. Ohmland: Wie schaffe ich das Examen? - Ein Beitrag zum Thema: Arbeits- und Kommunikationsstörungen von Studenten. (4) Arbeitsstörungen. (5) Kommunikationsstörungen. (6) Arbeitstechniken oder: Wie schaffe ich das Examen? - (C) K.-J. Kluge und A. von Kessel: "Lernen in Freiheit" - auch an der Erziehungswissenschaftlichen Fakultät der Universität zu Köln. (7) Zur Struktur der neuen Kompaktseminare. (8) Zu den pädagogischen Grundpositionen der Kölner Schule und ihren Forschungsergebnissen. (9) Zu den Persönlichkeitstheorien von Carl Rogers, Ruth Cohn und Thomas Gordon. (10) Ergebnisse der angewandten Persönlichkeitstheorien in der Hochschuldidaktik.
author: Kluge, Karl J.; Röben, Peter; Ohmland, Jörg; von Kessel, Anna

title: Problemlösetraining für Studienanfänger
abstract: In einer empirischen Studie wird die Effektivität eines Problemlösetrainings für Studienanfänger überprüft. Orientiert am Modell von D'Zurilla und Goldfried wurden drei Trainingsphasen unterschieden, in denen günstige Problemlöseschritte vorgestellt und anhand eigener Probleme der Teilnehmer eingeübt wurden: (1) Problemdefinition und -formulierunq; (2) Erstellen von Alternativen und Entscheiden; (3) Ueberpruefen. Das gesamte Training umfasste zehn Sitzungen zu je 100 Minuten. Drei Trainingsbedingungen wurden hergestellt: (1) Durchführung aller drei Trainingsphasen (acht Versuchspersonen); (2) Weglassen der Phase "Ueberpruefen" (sechs Versuchspersonen); (3) Weglassen der Phase "Problemdefinition und -formulierung" (sechs Versuchspersonen). Die acht Versuchspersonen einer vergleichbaren Kontrollgruppe hatten lediglich die entsprechenden Fragebögen zu den jeweiligen Messzeitpunkten auszufüllen. Zwei selbstkonstruierte Fragebögen dienten der Erfassung des individuellen Problemlöseverhaltens: einer mass die Überzeugung, vorgegebene relevante Problemsituationen aus dem Studienalltag angemessen lösen zu können, der andere erfasste die Fähigkeit, für ebenso relevante Problemsituationen effektive Lösungen gedanklich zu produzieren. Kontrollmessungen fanden vor und nach dem Training und nach Abschluss jeder Trainingsphase statt. Die statistische Auswertung erfolgte varianzanalytisch; multiple lineare Regressionsberechnungen dienten der Ermittlung der phasenspezifischen Effekte. Die Ergebnisse zeigten, dass das Training die Problemlösefähigkeit verbesserte. Die Phasen "Erstellen von Alternativen und Entscheiden" und "Problemdefinition und -formulierung" erwiesen sich als die wirksamsten; die Phase "Überprüfen" zeigte keinen Effekt. Damit ergab sich auch eine Überlegenheit der kognitionsorientierten Trainingsphasen gegenüber der verhaltensorientierten Phase ("Überprüfen").
author: Denk, Peter

title: Attitudes as factors of scholastic success
abstract: Chapter I defines terms and reviews 8 of 32 investigations that seemed to offer particularly valuable suggestions to the author. Chapter II deals with the securing of data from 260 students taking elementary educational psychology and from 113 students taking technique of teaching at the University of Illinois during the second semester of 1927-28. The following factors were studied: (1) previous training as measured by marks in prerequisite courses and scores on a specially constructed 'training test'; (2) intelligence as measured by the Brown University Psychological Examination; (3) reading ability as evidenced on specially constructed tests of rate and comprehension; (4) study habits (by questionnaire); and (5) attitudes (from ratings by instructors). The data are treated by zero order and partial correlation technique, from which it is concluded that the major factors of scholastic success are: (1) previous preparation; (2) intelligence; (3) study habits; (4) evaluative vs. non-evaluative attitude; (5) persevering vs. vascillating attitude; (6) self-confident vs. dependent attitude. The first five are related positively to scholastic success and the last negatively. An extensive bibliography is also presented. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2016 APA, all rights reserved)
author: Herriott, M. E.

title: Self-counseling for the college student
abstract: The University of Rochester's counseling plan furnishes the individual student with objective data upon which he may base his own decision. Counselors are available to explain the data, to suggest sources of information, and, when requested, to make positive suggestions. A battery of tests given during the first week of freshman year includes scholastic aptitude, reading comprehension, vocabulary, rate of reading, English fundamentals, and achievement in mathematics, chemistry, physics, French, and German.
